text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The head of a commercial TV station has asked for police protection after he was threatened following the broadcast of a programme about alleged criminal boss Henrikas Daktaras, currently on trial.
- Lithuanian lawmakers want to have the right to appoint the prosecutor general. The president currrently has that right.
- The government decided to increase the basic pension and the minimum living standard from February 1 but concrete sums are to decided at the next meeting of the cabinet.
- The payment for multi-entrance visa rose to $20 from $10.
- Finance Minister Rolandas Matiliauskas is against lower VAT for some food goods and fuel as VAT, normally 18 percent, is the main source of government revenue.
- Lithuanian Airlines is to increase ticket prices by three percent on January 10.
- The turnover of the state-owned Klaipeda sea port showed a 16 percent increase and it reloaded some 14.828 million cargos.
- The Lithuanian intellectual property copyright association collected 400,000 litas for the use of music copyrights. The main donors are radio stations, which pay two percent of their income.
- Foreign Minister Algirdas Saudargas urged the admission of at least one Baltic state during the first stage of NATO expansion to show guarantees for the future during his visit to Germany.
- Lithuanian celebrated the anniversary of the first book in Lithuanain, Katekizmas, by Martinas Mazvydas, published 450 years ago in Karaliaucius.
